items.title: Elon Musk, other tech execs sign petition calling on Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang
items.summary: A petition calling on Nvidia to reinstate ousted CEO Jensen Huang attracted more than 115,000 signatures as of Saturday afternoon, following Huang's resignation on Thursday. The petition website reported that signers included 5,965 current Nvidia employees, 1…
items.fullStory:
A petition calling on Nvidia to reinstate ousted CEO Jensen Huang attracted more than 115,000 signatures as of Saturday afternoon, following Huang's resignation on Thursday. The petition website reported that signers included 5,965 current Nvidia employees, 1,108 former employees, and 63,063 shareholders. Notable tech executives who signed the petition include Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, Replit CEO Amjad Masad, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan.

The petition states that signers are concerned Huang was removed without meaningful due process, demanding that the board bring him back while an independent investigation establishes the facts. The petition calls on the board to ensure a fair investigation, provide more information to the public, and asserts that Huang deserves due process rather than mob justice. Huang resigned four days after confessing to having an affair with a chip executive suspected by U.S. intelligence to be a Chinese spy, and he has agreed to testify before Congress amid news reports suggesting he engaged in multiple extramarital affairs.

Following Huang's departure, Nvidia appointed CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO while searching for a permanent replacement. Nvidia's stock price fell sharply throughout the week, and industry observers expect Huang's exit to leave a significant gap in AI industry funding.
items.whyItMatters: The leadership crisis at a central AI infrastructure giant like Nvidia, compounded by high-profile tech executive involvement, directly impacts market stability and AI startup funding ecosystems.
items.whoIsAffected: Nvidia employees, shareholders, tech executives, and stakeholders in the AI industry and startup funding ecosystem.

items.title: The AI graveyard: a running list of projects and startups that didn’t make it
items.summary: The AI industry has witnessed a wave of abandoned initiatives, pivots, and shutdowns, with S&P Global Market Intelligence estimating that about 42% of corporate AI initiatives are ultimately abandoned due to funding shortages, technical challenges, competitio…
items.fullStory:
The AI industry has witnessed a wave of abandoned initiatives, pivots, and shutdowns, with S&P Global Market Intelligence estimating that about 42% of corporate AI initiatives are ultimately abandoned due to funding shortages, technical challenges, competition, scaling difficulties, or weak user demand. Prominent industry players like OpenAI have experienced multiple casualties, such as a July 9 app redesign that combined features into a cluttered "super app" interface before being rolled back, the discontinuation of the ChatGPT Atlas web browser on August 9, and the March 2026 shutdown of the Sora video-sharing platform due to high operating costs and low user retention. Other high-profile casualties include Apple's delayed Siri AI feature—which faced engineering issues and bugs, contributing to a $250 million marketing-claims settlement—and consumer chatbot platform Character.ai, which filed for bankruptcy in early October 2026 after facing legal and regulatory headwinds, including lawsuits alleging chatbots contributed to teen suicides and a Disney cease-and-desist letter. Disney emerged as the opening bidder offering $20 million for Character.ai's intellectual property license.

Additional product failures and shutdowns span automation tools, hardware devices, and niche apps. Workflow automation tool Relay shut down in August 2026 after struggling to compete with built-in platform features, while privacy-focused household assistant Ollie announced its shutdown on November 6, 2026, citing capital and growth challenges. Microsoft's Recall feature faced heavy privacy backlash over creating a searchable archive of sensitive digital history, resulting in prolonged delays and lingering security questions. Notion Mail was scheduled to shut down on September 22 after users preferred separate AI agents for their inboxes. Hardware failures included the Humane AI Pin shutting down its business in February 2025 due to performance struggles and battery fire risks, with its assets sold to HP for $116 million, while the Rabbit R1 faced criticism for unfinished performance before pivoting toward computer controller tasks and a new "Project Cyberdeck" hardware project.

Further casualties include Huxe, an AI audio app built by former Google NotebookLM developers that shut down in May 2026 as larger platforms expanded audio tools, and Yupp, a multi-model testing playground that shut down in March 2026 after failing to achieve product-market fit. Figgs AI similarly shut down between 2023 and 2024 because maintaining a free customizable character role-play platform became too expensive. These closures highlight the intense competitive pressures, high operating costs, and market hurdles faced by early-stage AI startups and standalone products as major platforms absorb similar native features.
items.whyItMatters: This comprehensive overview illustrates how intense competition, high operating costs, and changing user demands are reshaping the AI landscape, forcing even major tech companies and heavily funded startups to shutter products or file for bankruptcy.
items.whoIsAffected: AI startup founders, product developers, enterprise technology investors, and consumer software users.

items.title: Asian governments react to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s exit
items.summary: Following the departure of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, Asian governments have responded with a range of measures concerning chip supply commitments, local project impacts, and ongoing investigations. On Sunday, November 8, Nvidia’s board launched an independent…
items.fullStory:
Following the departure of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, Asian governments have responded with a range of measures concerning chip supply commitments, local project impacts, and ongoing investigations. On Sunday, November 8, Nvidia’s board launched an independent investigation after reports that Huang was targeted by a Chinese spy operation, during which Huang admitted to an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based chip company Megaspeed. Nvidia’s leadership change has generated widespread uncertainty and reactions across key Asian markets heavily reliant on the chipmaker's hardware and partnerships.

In China, the foreign ministry rejected allegations on November 10 that a Chinese businesswoman linked to Huang was a spy, calling them groundless smears, while reiterating opposition to export controls. Reuters reported that Huang's exit created uncertainty over more than $3 billion in Chinese AI computing projects reliant on restricted Nvidia processors. In Singapore, the Ministry of Home Affairs detailed that authorities seized the passport of Alice Huang in June 2025 during an investigation into possible false declarations regarding server purchases. Although police found insufficient evidence of offenses related to false declarations in February 2026, she was issued a warning and barred from re-entering Singapore after providing inaccurate information about her role at Megaspeed, with investigations into six other individuals remaining ongoing.

Elsewhere in the region, South Korea's Science Ministry stated that Nvidia reaffirmed plans to supply 260,000 advanced GPUs to the country and continue joint AI projects, while South Korea's government AI strategy council held an emergency meeting to assess the departure's impact. In Taiwan, Economy Minister Kung Ming-shin stated the departure was unlikely to significantly alter global AI industry growth, and Taipei officials confirmed Nvidia's planned overseas headquarters remains on track. In Japan, the Industry Ministry announced it would closely monitor Nvidia, with Deputy Chief Cabinet Secretary Masanao Ozaki noting it was too early to assess the global impact while emphasizing commitment to a stable semiconductor supply.
items.whyItMatters: The sudden departure of Nvidia's CEO and the accompanying geopolitical fallout directly impact international supply chains, billions of dollars in AI infrastructure projects, and semiconductor strategies across major Asian economies.
items.whoIsAffected: Government officials, policymakers, chipmakers like Samsung and SK Hynix, and tech industry stakeholders across China, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, and Japan.

items.title: Jensen Huang’s departure blasts big hole in AI startup funding, VCs and founders say
items.summary: On November 13, 2026, TechCrunch reported that Jensen Huang officially stepped down after leading Nvidia for 33 years. VCs and founders described the departure as a major shock to the AI startup ecosystem, leaving a significant funding void since Nvidia had p…
items.fullStory:
On November 13, 2026, TechCrunch reported that Jensen Huang officially stepped down after leading Nvidia for 33 years. VCs and founders described the departure as a major shock to the AI startup ecosystem, leaving a significant funding void since Nvidia had participated in 105 investment rounds that year and poured tens of billions of dollars annually into startups. Investors noted that most of the significant investment decisions came directly from Huang, and his absence leaves young companies without one of their biggest champions.

Nvidia's interim CEO, Colette Kress, is expected to take a more conservative approach and scale back early-stage startup investments, particularly regarding the expensive data center build-outs, neoclouds, inference providers, and open-weight models that Huang heavily backed. Nvidia's historical investments included backing CoreWeave while private, participating in Crusoe's $1.4 billion Series E, agreeing to buy Hugging Face for $13 billion, and writing an $800 million check into Reflection AI's $2 billion Series B. Market participants warned that the loss of Nvidia's aggressive support, especially for open-source initiatives and European startups, creates an ecosystem gap that other entities cannot easily fill.

While Nvidia's generous funding effectively locked startups into using its chips and CUDA software platform, its presence on cap tables provided comfort for traditional venture capitalists to back high-valuation infrastructure companies. Without Nvidia's substantial checks, valuations are expected to drop and traditional VCs may pause certain dealmaking. Although investors hope that Big Tech rivals like Google, Amazon, Microsoft, and AMD might step in, many doubt these competitors will pour hundreds of millions into pre-revenue infrastructure startups the way Nvidia did under Huang.
items.whyItMatters: Jensen Huang's resignation removes Nvidia's prolific startup-funding engine, threatening to disrupt AI valuations, dealmaking, and the early-stage infrastructure ecosystem.
items.whoIsAffected: AI startup founders, venture capitalists, neocloud providers, and open-source AI developers.

items.title: AI agent startup LangChain hits $3B valuation
items.summary: AI agent startup LangChain announced on Friday that it has raised a $300 million Series C funding round led by CapitalG, pushing the company's valuation to $3 billion. Additional participation in the funding round came from Singapore’s GIC, DFJ Growth, IVP, a…
items.fullStory:
AI agent startup LangChain announced on Friday that it has raised a $300 million Series C funding round led by CapitalG, pushing the company's valuation to $3 billion. Additional participation in the funding round came from Singapore’s GIC, DFJ Growth, IVP, and Sapphire Ventures. This new valuation is more than double the $1.25 billion valuation LangChain achieved about a year prior when it raised $125 million in a round also led by IVP.

Originally launched in 2022 as an open-source project designed to help early-stage large language models handle tasks like web searching, API calls, and database interaction, LangChain shifted its focus toward managing AI agents as frontier AI labs integrated those capabilities natively. The company now positions its agent creation and management software, LangSmith, around a strategy of letting businesses own their own intelligence without locking them into any specific model, cloud, or ecosystem. Furthermore, the platform promises to contain agent behavior while remaining easy to use.

Despite competing in a crowded sector alongside newer startups like Mintive, LangChain has leveraged its head start to build a customer base of 7,000 LangSmith users. This roster includes prominent startups such as Harvey, Rippling, and Clay, as well as major enterprises like Nvidia, Toyota, and Salesforce.
items.whyItMatters: LangChain's massive $300 million raise and $3 billion valuation highlight intense investor confidence and capital flow into agentic AI management platforms. This funding underscores the growing enterprise demand for vendor-neutral tools to build, manage, and monitor AI agents securely.
items.whoIsAffected: Enterprise organizations, tech startups, and developers building and managing AI agents using LangChain's platform.

items.title: Export-banned Nvidia chips are behind China’s most powerful AI models — uh-oh, Jensen!
items.summary: A new research effort by Will DePue, a former OpenAI researcher leading the nonprofit Unemployment Labs, claims that leading open-weight models developed by Chinese companies were trained on Nvidia chips restricted from export by the U.S. government. DePue an…
items.fullStory:
A new research effort by Will DePue, a former OpenAI researcher leading the nonprofit Unemployment Labs, claims that leading open-weight models developed by Chinese companies were trained on Nvidia chips restricted from export by the U.S. government. DePue analyzed the weights of large language models released openly by DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax, and Ant Group, finding evidence that models including Moonshot's Kimi K3 releases and DeepSeek's V4 bear fingerprints from training on Blackwell chips. White House technology adviser Michael Kratsios previously stated that Moonshot had used export-banned Nvidia chips, while Epoch AI estimates about two million advanced chips entered China in 2024 and 2025 through smuggling schemes, including 275,000 imported to Malaysia.

The widespread access to Blackwell GPUs highlights challenges in U.S. export controls, which prohibit exporting the chips to China or Chinese-owned firms directly, though the Trump administration permits H200 chip exports via circuitous routes with a 25% tariff. Smuggling operations have been tied to Megaspeed, a company led by Alice Huang, whose subsidiary Speedmatrix has been investigated by U.S. and Singaporean authorities. Bloomberg reported that a company linked to Alice Huang helped smuggle banned Nvidia chips to a Shanghai data center. Additionally, short-selling firm Culper previously published a report in May detailing Megaspeed's relationship with Nvidia and alleging that Alice Huang's companies are backed by barred Chinese firms.

In the wake of these developments, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang left the company after admitting to an affair with Alice Huang, an executive of Megaspeed who is also alleged to be an agent of China's intelligence service. Nvidia's potential corporate liability for export control violations factored into the decision to part ways with Huang, despite Nvidia officials previously visiting Megaspeed data centers to confirm their legitimacy. Meanwhile, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick faces scrutiny and potential job loss after reports that his investigators failed to uncover suspicious buyers and were too cozy with Nvidia officials, leaving questions about future U.S. oversight of high-performance AI chip distribution.
items.whyItMatters: The revelation that Chinese AI labs are successfully utilizing export-banned Nvidia chips highlights major loopholes in U.S. geopolitical export controls and triggers leadership upheaval at the world's most critical chipmaker.
items.whoIsAffected: Nvidia executives, U.S. government trade regulators, and Chinese artificial intelligence frontier labs.

items.title: Build a Robot Pick-and-Place Simulation with SimReady Assets
items.summary: On November 13, 2026, Dillon Bailey, Pomi Lee, and Rishabh Chadha published a tutorial walkthrough on Hugging Face detailing how to build a robot pick-and-place simulation using SimReady assets. The guide demonstrates composing a scene in Isaac Sim 6.2 using…
items.fullStory:
On November 13, 2026, Dillon Bailey, Pomi Lee, and Rishabh Chadha published a tutorial walkthrough on Hugging Face detailing how to build a robot pick-and-place simulation using SimReady assets. The guide demonstrates composing a scene in Isaac Sim 6.2 using a UR17G arm, a Robotiq 2F-140 gripper, and a beverage can, leveraging agent-generated controls from a frontier AI model such as GPT-6 Sol. SimReady assets provide OpenUSD files prepared with predefined simulation properties such as collisions, mass, joints, and joint drives, allowing developers to reuse validated components from the open SimReady Central asset library on Hugging Face.

The walkthrough outlines a three-step process: downloading the necessary assets from SimReady Central, assembling the robot components and validating their physics, and testing the controls to execute a pick-and-place task. The arm validation report utilizes the Robot-Body 4.0.0 profile, while the gripper report uses Robot-Gripper 3.0.0, both confirming passing PhysX driven-joint checks. The assembly and execution process uses bundled agent skills in Isaac Sim 6.2, such as 'isaac-sim-remote', 'usd-articulation', 'manipulaiton-ik', and 'physics-simulation', enabling the AI agent to interact with the simulation via Python.

Key simulation assumptions for the task include a fixed setup with a known starting position, no vision integration, and a simplified can model without deformation or liquid motion. A horizontal grasp uses a 2 N·m drive-effort cap determined through simulation tests rather than manufacturer calibration. The authors note that these results apply strictly to the scripted setup and do not establish hardware robustness. Developers are encouraged to use the tutorial to build their own simulations, contribute assets to SimReady Central, and share results in the Hugging Face comments.
items.whyItMatters: This walkthrough demonstrates how developers can combine OpenUSD-based SimReady assets from Hugging Face with AI agents and Isaac Sim to rapidly build and validate robotic pick-and-place simulations.
items.whoIsAffected: Robotics engineers, simulation developers, and AI practitioners building automation workflows.

items.title: XYBench: Helping with the problem behind the question
items.summary: Kyle Wiggers published an article on Hugging Face on November 13, 2026, announcing the release of XYBench, a benchmark designed to test how AI assistants handle the "XY problem." The XY problem occurs when a user wants to achieve a goal (X), assumes a specifi…
items.fullStory:
Kyle Wiggers published an article on Hugging Face on November 13, 2026, announcing the release of XYBench, a benchmark designed to test how AI assistants handle the "XY problem." The XY problem occurs when a user wants to achieve a goal (X), assumes a specific approach (Y) will work, and asks for help with Y based on a misconception. Developed in collaboration with researchers at Carnegie Mellon University, NVIDIA, and Johns Hopkins, XYBench won the Best Resource Paper Award at EMNLP 2026. The benchmark comprises 8,115 real-world questions from four sources: 1,557 from Stack Overflow, 184 from Stack Exchange, 102 manually curated examples, and 6,272 generated from WikiHow guides spanning programming, cooking, and home repair.

The authors evaluated five models on XYBench in a single-turn setting: Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Qwen3.5-9B, and DeepSeek-V4 Pro. The evaluations revealed that all five models were more likely to include a solution to the stated request (Y) than to the underlying goal (X). For example, on Stack Overflow, stated-request solutions appeared in 75% to 86% of responses, compared to 59% to 71% for underlying-goal solutions. Furthermore, models focused primarily on the underlying goal in only 35% to 41% of their Stack Overflow responses, favoring the stated request in 47% to 57% of cases, unlike human reference answers which better steered users away from mistaken approaches.

In an oracle experiment where both the stated request and intended request were supplied to the models, Sonnet 4.6's rate of including an underlying-goal solution rose from 59% to 67%, but its misconception-identification rate fell from 47% to 34%. A separate evaluation testing models as judges found that when presented with two possible answers—one literal and one goal-focused—all six models (including GPT-4.1) chose the goal-focused answer in 71% to 84% of cases. This demonstrated a distinct gap between a model's ability to recognize useful advice and its ability to autonomously produce it.

Looking ahead, the creators hope XYBench will enable researchers to measure whether model improvements and training methods help assistants better recognize mistaken assumptions and prioritize effective solutions. Future work aims to extend XYBench beyond English-language queries and procedural problems to other languages, cultures, and conversational settings.
items.whyItMatters: XYBench exposes a critical capability gap in leading LLMs, showing they struggle to look past user misconceptions and prioritize solutions for underlying goals compared to humans.
items.whoIsAffected: AI researchers, developers building AI assistants, and end users relying on LLMs for troubleshooting.

Furthermore, customers can still earn credit card rewards and use standard card protections like transaction disputes.

To begin, subscribers add eligible payment cards to the ChatGPT Wallet once and then ask their dot to assist with purchases. Merchants automatically receive fulfillment details such as shipping addresses and contact information from the dot. OpenAI noted that the initial limited rollout is designed to test and improve capabilities before a wider release.

Looking ahead, OpenAI plans to introduce features allowing users to set spending limits and configure parameters for purchase categories or time periods, enabling more autonomous agent transactions. items.title: The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline
items.summary: Nvidia co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang faced a major scandal in late 2026 after admitting to multiple extramarital affairs, including relationships linked to national security concerns and internal company governance. U.S. officials suspected that one of Huan…
items.fullStory:
Nvidia co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang faced a major scandal in late 2026 after admitting to multiple extramarital affairs, including relationships linked to national security concerns and internal company governance. U.S. officials suspected that one of Huang's romantic interests, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang (no relation), was a Chinese spy feeding information to Beijing and illegally routing advanced chips to China. Following public revelations, internal investigations, and dropping stock prices, Huang resigned from his post on November 11, 2026, with CFO Colette Kress stepping in as interim CEO while Harvey C. Jones was appointed as the board's first-ever chair.

The scandal escalated rapidly as additional reports from The New York Times and Reuters revealed further affairs with Nvidia vice president of healthcare Kimberly Powell and an unnamed third employee. Concurrently, political pressure mounted rapidly as Democratic lawmakers launched investigations into how the Trump administration handled Nvidia's chip sales to China, and Republican committee chairmen demanded congressional testimony. Huang agreed to testify before Congress in a closed-door session prior to Thanksgiving, while facing fallout over export controls, national security risks, and the company's lack of a clear succession plan.

As the fallout continued, reports highlighted internal friction, noting that Huang had previously criticized Kress as "a deer in the headlights" and appeared visibly depleted upon surrendering his leadership role. Nvidia's stock suffered significant drops in after-hours trading, and the Department of Justice took over the federal investigation into Megaspeed. Meanwhile, leaders across various congressional committees pressed forward with probes into the extent of foreign infiltration and access to critical U.S. AI hardware.
items.whyItMatters: The sudden resignation of Nvidia's CEO amid national security investigations and export control controversies threatens to destabilize a central pillar of the global AI hardware supply chain. The unfolding situation invites intense legislative scrutiny over how the U.S. manages sensitive technology transfers to foreign adversaries during a critical technological arms race.

items.fullStory:
On November 13, 2026, the team behind llama.cpp—including contributors Daniel Bevenius, Georgi Gerganov, and Merve Noyan—announced the release of llama.cpp v1.0.0 and ggml v1.0.0. Spanning 3.5 years since its inception, the project provides a lightweight, versatile platform for running multi-modal LLMs across various hardware configurations, from consumer-grade machines to enterprise servers, utilizing quantization, optimized backends, and portable C/C++ implementations.

The v1.0.0 release establishes stable library interfaces (libllama and libggml) with explicit semantic versioning rules, ensuring that future API and ABI incompatibilities will be clearly communicated through major-version bumps. This stability addresses the needs of downstream applications and developers relying on the library interfaces as local AI and privacy grow in importance.

The underlying machine learning engine, ggml, currently supports over 150 architecture variants and all mainstream speculative decoding methods across hardware backends from NVIDIA, AMD, Qualcomm, Arm, IBM, and Intel. Distribution channels include Linux, macOS, Windows, Android, and iOS via packages such as Docker, Homebrew, conda-forge, MacPorts, and Winget.

Moving forward, the project plans to expand distribution pathways and utilize Hugging Face technologies like HF Buckets and HF Jobs to scale continuous integration infrastructure and guarantee correctness across master branches.
items.whyItMatters: The release of v1.0.0 provides a stable API and ABI foundation for developers building privacy-focused, cross-platform local AI applications across diverse hardware backends. Richard Neal (D-Mass.), top Democrat on the House Ways and Means Committee, and Sen. Ron Wyden (D-Ore.), top Democrat on the Senate Finance Committee, who sent a scathing letter to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick asking the department to preserve records regarding an arrangement they allege is illegal. items.title: Dispelling LTAP myths
items.summary: In a November 12, 2026 engineering blog post titled "Dispelling LTAP myths," Sergey Melnik addressed common misconceptions surrounding Lakebase's Lake Table Analytics Platform (LTAP) architecture. Melnik explained that LTAP establishes the lake as the primary…
items.fullStory:
In a November 12, 2026 engineering blog post titled "Dispelling LTAP myths," Sergey Melnik addressed common misconceptions surrounding Lakebase's Lake Table Analytics Platform (LTAP) architecture. Melnik explained that LTAP establishes the lake as the primary database storage rather than a replica, utilizing one Delta or Iceberg table and one catalog, with Postgres caches and pageservers positioned in front for speed. According to the post, point lookups read Postgres heap pages while scans read Parquet, ensuring that every analytical query encounters a consistent snapshot, including recent commits not yet materialized in the lake.

The commentary following Reynold Xin's earlier post, "From monolith to Lakebase to LTAP," generated four primary myths that Melnik systematically refuted. The first myth claims that LTAP is simply CDC or logical replication under another name. Melnik clarified that LTAP maintains one durable copy in the lake rather than a second database catalog, distinguishing a tiered caching architecture from replication. The second myth argues that a single data copy forces either slow point lookups or slow scans. Melnik countered this by explaining that LTAP utilizes two lossless encodings over the same rows—Postgres heap pages for point lookups and Parquet for analytical scans.

The third myth assumes open table formats on object storage are inherently stale and cause analytical queries to see eventual consistency. Melnik explained that queries avoid this lag by reading materialized data from object storage up to a specific Log Sequence Number (LSN) watermark, while pageservers dynamically supply any newer commits not yet in the lake. The fourth myth suggests that standard Postgres logical replication is already sufficient for analytics. Melnik argued that logical replication is a costly and resource-intensive method because it forces pipelines to replay every change row by row.

Moving forward, the post notes that APIs for reading recent changes since a watermark are actively being developed both natively for Lakebase and as an extension for upstream Postgres. These developments aim to solidify LTAP's ability to serve unified transactional and analytical workloads without the overhead of traditional ETL or CDC pipelines.
items.whyItMatters: This post clarifies the architectural foundations of Lakebase's LTAP design, showing how object storage and open table formats can serve both transactional and analytical workloads without traditional replication pipelines. This directly addresses industry skepticism regarding consistency, performance, and storage overhead in modern lakehouse databases.

items.title: Nebius tests the neocloud playbook with $40 billion in planned spending
items.summary: During its third-quarter earnings call on Thursday, neocloud company Nebius announced plans for $40 billion in planned spending for 2027, surpassing Wall Street expectations. CEO Arkady Volozh addressed the challenges of rapid infrastructure development, stat…
items.fullStory:
During its third-quarter earnings call on Thursday, neocloud company Nebius announced plans for $40 billion in planned spending for 2027, surpassing Wall Street expectations. CEO Arkady Volozh addressed the challenges of rapid infrastructure development, stating, “Building at this scale is hard, and delays are part of our industry right now. We are not immune.” The company intends to fund its buildout using customer prepayments and loans backed by customer contracts, though this strategy carries risks if projects encounter delays or cancellations.

A key test for Nebius involves its partnership with Microsoft, which is paying up to $19.4 billion for AI computing capacity at a Vineland, New Jersey, data center that is currently months behind schedule. Andrey Korolenko, chief product and infrastructure officer, explained that only just over half of the Microsoft capacity will be delivered by the end of the year, with the remainder pushed to Q2 2027 because third-party operator DataOne wound down temporary power generation faster than expected to transition to Bloom Energy fuel cells. The site previously faced regulatory scrutiny when investigative site Floodlight identified 45 unpermitted natural gas generators, resulting in a $1.1 million fine from New Jersey regulators for violating federal law, alongside a noise-complaint lawsuit from local residents.

Under the contract terms, Microsoft can terminate affected services after a grace period if deadlines are missed without alternative capacity, and the agreement includes financial penalties for late delivery. Chief revenue officer Marc Boroditsky noted that deals with Microsoft and Meta included significant prepayments, and CFO Maria Del Dado Alonso Sanchez stated that prepayments and asset-backed financing are expected to cover up to 85% of the $40 to $45 billion 2027 capital expenditure. Amid these project delays, Nebius cut its 2026 revenue forecast by $200 million to $3 billion—reporting Q3 revenue of $981 million, which was up 571% year-over-year—while forecasting 2027 revenue between $12 billion and $13 billion and a pre-tax break-even by the fourth quarter. Following the announcements, Nebius shares closed down 17%.
items.whyItMatters: Nebius' massive $40 billion spending plan and delayed third-party data center projects highlight the escalating financial and operational risks neoclouds face as major tech clients like Microsoft tighten oversight on AI infrastructure delivery.
items.whoIsAffected: Nebius executives, investors, and major AI infrastructure clients including Microsoft and Meta.

items.title: Google’s latest Search upgrade promises better answers to your most complicated questions

items.fullStory:
Google announced a major Search upgrade on November 12, 2026, powered by its newly released Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, which the company describes as its biggest model improvement to Search yet. Authored by Sarah Perez, the announcement details how Hydrogen is designed for fast execution across agentic workflows, completing tasks 2.5 times faster than the previous Gemini 3.8 Flash model while beating the more powerful Gemini 4 Argon on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index benchmark at its default high thinking level. Google stated that Hydrogen enables Search to better handle complicated, multi-part questions, natural trains of thought, and hard-to-understand typos by improving intent understanding, tool usage, and the fan-out technique that breaks prompts into subqueries.

In addition to textual enhancements, the integration of Hydrogen brings more images, structured responses, comparison tables, and custom tools to Search's AI Mode. The model features four thinking levels—low, medium, high (default), and an extra-high tier ("xhigh")—and ranks No. 5 on Agent Arena's benchmarks for multi-step tasks like deep research, data analysis, and codebase navigation. Google noted that Hydrogen can operate independently for everyday tasks such as writing code and running tests, or work alongside frontier models like Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon in combined workflows.

Beyond Google Search, Gemini 4 Hydrogen is rolling out globally to all Search users and is expanding to all tiers of Google's AI Studio, the Gemini API, the Gemini App, and paid AI Pro and Ultra subscribers on the Antigravity development platform. Google explained that the release stems from the realization that users do not always require the deepest reasoning models for everyday execution, making a faster, cheaper, and reasonably smart alternative viable for a wide range of applications.

Written by Renee Voves and Herman Lombard, the article explains that while Constellation's teams built strong individual data capabilities, cross-domain questions lacked shared definitions, a problem compounded by its 2026 acquisition of Calpine, which brought 79 power plants across 22 states and 27 GW of capacity into the fold.

Constellation selected Databricks because it interoperates with existing architecture rather than forcing a rip-and-replace. The EDP is built on three architectural pillars: shared conforming semantics to reconcile differing definitions across retail, wholesale, and CRM; Unity Catalog for lineage, fine-grained access control, metric views, and defining data ownership; and multi-workspaces on a single governed foundation. Using this unified foundation, Constellation is developing early AI use cases, including a nuclear engineering assistant built with Databricks Genie, an outage planning tool to coordinate complex nuclear maintenance, and sales intelligence capabilities for opportunity prioritization.

Looking forward, Constellation is exploring Genie Ontology, a self-learning knowledge graph, and Unity Catalog Pages to centrally manage business definitions. The initiative is supported by leaders Jay Cavalcanto, SVP & CIO, and Vineeth Vijaykumar, VP of the IT Business Management Office.

The announcement arrives as U.S. spending on creator advertising is projected to reach $44 billion in 2026, according to the Interactive Advertising Bureau.

The Creator Agent searches over 300 million creator profiles across Instagram and TikTok, analyzing videos and brand safety context to provide ranked lists of recommendations. CEO Misbah Uraizee stated that the agent uses proprietary guardrails and brand voice guidelines to draft personalized messages, manage contracts, and track product gifting. Additionally, the agent monitors personal milestones in creators' lives, such as engagements or new babies, to suggest personalized messages or gifts for relationship building.

Creator Agent is available globally starting November 12, 2026, and covers Instagram and TikTok creators. items.title: LLMON: An LLM-Native Markup Language, now in Granite 4.1 3B and 8B
items.summary: On November 12, 2026, researchers from IBM Granite, including Abraham Daniels, Basel Shbita, Chad DeLuca, Dan Gutfreund, Michael Hind, and Shub A, released LLMON (LLM Object Notation, pronounced "lemon"), an LLM-native markup language designed to explicitly c…
items.fullStory:
On November 12, 2026, researchers from IBM Granite, including Abraham Daniels, Basel Shbita, Chad DeLuca, Dan Gutfreund, Michael Hind, and Shub A, released LLMON (LLM Object Notation, pronounced "lemon"), an LLM-native markup language designed to explicitly communicate structure and semantics to causal language models. Alongside the markup language, the team released two experimental preview models derived from Granite 4.1 base checkpoints—`granite-4.1-3b-LLMON-preview` and `granite-4.1-8b-LLMON-preview`—along with a GitHub repository containing a toolkit, templates, and workflow examples.

Traditional LLMs rely on implicit context and formats like JSON, which were designed for parsers rather than causal language models, making smaller models brittle and vulnerable to prompt injection. LLMON addresses this by using XML-like markup with reserved special tokens for structural delimiters, unambiguous data schemas, unique IDs, and explicit instruction-and-data separation. In evaluations on the OPI, ASB, and StruQ benchmarks, LLMON models practically eliminated static indirect prompt injection, avoiding 47% more attacks than the best tested frontier model and 95% more than the best open-source model, while maintaining general capabilities on par with Granite 4.1 Instruct models. The training process utilized Granite 4.1 base checkpoints, re-serializing instruction-tuning corpora into LLMON blocks, followed by reinforcement learning via five sequential GRPO stages and a final DPO stage on preference pairs.

The developers also released JSON-to-LLMON lossless conversion tools, native support in Mellea, and a Hugging Face Space for LLMON Attention Visualization. Furthermore, the team demonstrated domain adaptability using a LoRA adapter on the ScienceWorld benchmark, proving that users can define custom tag vocabularies tailored to specific application domains.
items.whyItMatters: LLMON introduces an LLM-native markup alternative to JSON that fundamentally solves structural ambiguity and drastically reduces indirect prompt injection vulnerabilities without sacrificing model capability.
items.whoIsAffected: AI developers, software engineers, and security teams building applications with LLMs.

items.title: Jensen Huang’s exit puts Nvidia’s support for open source in question
items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday, November 12, 2026, after admitting to an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. The departure raises national security concerns regarding Huang's past advocacy for softer chip export controls on China. Nvidia named C…
items.fullStory:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday, November 12, 2026, after admitting to an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. The departure raises national security concerns regarding Huang's past advocacy for softer chip export controls on China. Nvidia named CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO, leaving the future of the company's open source commitments and pending acquisitions uncertain.

Huang was a leading advocate for open source AI, framing the ecosystem as beneficial for safety, innovation, diffusion, and sovereignty. Under his leadership, Nvidia pushed for the development of the Nemotron family of open-weight AI models, backed startups like Reflection AI and Thinking Machines Lab, and agreed to a $6 billion non-exclusive licensing deal for Poolside's technology. Additionally, Nvidia has yet to finalize a pending $13 billion acquisition of open source platform Hugging Face. Huang also led an open letter earlier in the year, signed by 25 companies including Microsoft, Meta, IBM, and Palantir, urging the U.S. government not to over-restrict open-weight AI models.

Without Huang, open source community members express concern that new leadership may take a more cautious approach, potentially downgrading founder-driven priorities. The scandal and leadership change could also strengthen arguments in Washington for tougher restrictions on Chinese AI companies and open-weight models, shifting the balance against closed-model advocates like Anthropic and OpenAI. Despite Huang's exit, Nvidia retains underlying business incentives to support an open ecosystem to diversify its customer base away from a handful of frontier labs and sell more GPUs.
items.whyItMatters: Jensen Huang's sudden resignation creates uncertainty around Nvidia's massive investments in open source AI, its pending $13 billion acquisition of Hugging Face, and Washington's ongoing policy debates over open-weight models and export controls.
items.whoIsAffected: Open source AI developers, Nvidia employees, and policymakers navigating U.S. export controls and AI regulations.

items.fullStory:
On November 12, 2026, Hugging Face CEO Clément Delangue publicly commented on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure, calling it a "really sad day" and stating on X that "This whole thing sucks, and I wish none of it had happened." He reassured open-source advocates by vowing that Hugging Face will keep fighting for open-source AI harder than ever. Nvidia had previously announced plans in September to acquire Hugging Face for $12.9 billion, marking the second-largest acquisition in Nvidia's history behind its purchase of chipmaker Groq's assets for $20 billion in December 2025.

Huang's exit raised concerns among open-source advocates because he had been a strong champion for open-source AI and open-weight models. Following the acquisition announcement, the U.S. Department of Justice began inquiries in October regarding how the deal would impact market competition. Meanwhile, the Hugging Face acquisition remains scheduled to close in the first half of 2027, with requests for comment on the deal status and interim CEO Colette Kress unreturned.

Huang's advocacy included publishing an AI policy letter in July signed by 25 companies—including Microsoft, Meta, Hugging Face, IBM, and Palantir—urging the U.S. government not to over-restrict open-weight models. Additionally, Nvidia announced a $6 billion deal with coding startup Poolside in August to build an open AI ecosystem, expanded its Nemotron open-weight model family last month, and promoted open-source AI during his January keynote address at the Consumer Electronics Show.
items.whyItMatters: Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia creates uncertainty for the future of open-source AI initiatives and the pending $12.9 billion Hugging Face acquisition, prompting reassurances from leadership.
items.whoIsAffected: Open-source AI advocates, Hugging Face users, and developers relying on open-weight models.

items.title: Lakehouse//RT: Scale real-time analytics, not your bill
items.summary: On November 12, 2026, Databricks engineering authors JooHo Yeo and Kaitlin Baumgardner highlighted Lakehouse//RT in a blog post, positioning it as a solution for managing high-volume real-time analytics driven by AI agents. Traditional data warehouses often s…
items.fullStory:
On November 12, 2026, Databricks engineering authors JooHo Yeo and Kaitlin Baumgardner highlighted Lakehouse//RT in a blog post, positioning it as a solution for managing high-volume real-time analytics driven by AI agents. Traditional data warehouses often see costs scale linearly with query volume, which poses a financial challenge when AI agents generate hundreds of queries per second around the clock. Lakehouse//RT is designed to absorb this increased demand without proportional cost increases by scaling efficiency rather than raw capacity.

The system achieves its cost efficiency through four key pillars: high concurrency support, faster query execution, small-increment autoscaling, and unification into a single system rather than relying on separate serving layers. According to the company, Lakehouse//RT can deliver sub-100 millisecond latency at 12,000 queries per second. Through January 2027, Databricks is offering a 30% discount for users trying Lakehouse//RT in beta.

Early adopters have reported significant gains. Aurasell transitioned from multiple clusters at 200 queries per second to a single small Lakehouse//RT warehouse supporting over 250 QPS with 4-5x faster execution and a 10x cost reduction, as noted by CTO Srinivas Bandi. VisionHeight achieved a greater than 90% cost reduction and 3x faster response times after replacing Apache Pinot within a three-day migration, according to CTO and Co-founder Nitsan Daniel. Additionally, nOps cut infrastructure costs by over 6x and eliminated 40TB of duplicated data by replacing Apache Druid, according to Director of Engineering Jordan Stein.

Next steps for organizations include spinning up a new Lakehouse//RT warehouse in beta to test demanding real-time workloads, reviewing pricing details, and consulting account teams to model cost impacts for specific workloads.
items.whyItMatters: Lakehouse//RT addresses the unsustainable cost scaling of traditional data warehouses under high-volume AI agent queries by unifying real-time serving directly on the lakehouse. This allows organizations to run thousands of concurrent queries with sub-100ms latency while cutting infrastructure costs by 6x to 10x.
items.whoIsAffected: Data engineers, architects, and engineering leaders building real-time dashboards and AI agent applications.

items.summary: On November 12, 2026, Hugging Face authors Suvaditya Mukherjee, Merve Noyan, and Pedro Cuenca published a definitive guide and accompanying scripts and containers for fine-tuning TRELLIS.2, a popular 3D generation model. The release provides tools for users t…

On November 12, 2026, Hugging Face authors Suvaditya Mukherjee, Merve Noyan, and Pedro Cuenca published a definitive guide and accompanying scripts and containers for fine-tuning TRELLIS.2, a popular 3D generation model. The release provides tools for users to fine-tune the model on custom 3D assets either locally or via Hugging Face Jobs. While general-purpose models like TRELLIS.2 generate functional 3D objects, they can produce inaccurate details for specific applications, such as flawed shoe soles when generating footwear. To address this, the guide demonstrates using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) via Hugging Face's PEFT library on a subset of the Google Scanned Objects (GSO) dataset containing 188 footwear objects.

The TRELLIS.2 pipeline operates in five main stages: background removal via BiRefNet, image encoding via DINOv3-L, sparse structure generation using a diffusion transformer (DiT), geometry generation via a shape flow DiT, and material generation combined with mesh creation. The fine-tuning guide advises freezing the texture flow DiT to prevent catastrophic forgetting due to lack of proper material maps, and instead applying LoRA adapters solely to the sparse-structure flow DiT (using rank 8 adapters totaling approximately 9.3 million parameters across both targeted DiTs) and the shape flow DiT (using rank 16 adapters in attention layers).

To execute the workflow, users utilize two Docker images for preprocessing and training, which can be run locally or via Hugging Face Jobs using hardware such as an A100-large instance. The preprocessing container utilizes Blender to render 16 views per object and formats meshes into the latent representations required by TRELLIS.2, taking about one hour for the 188-object footwear dataset. The training container then runs the fine-tuning jobs for the sparse-structure ("ss") and shape ("shape") modes, recording metrics with Trackio and uploading final adapter checkpoints to the Hugging Face Hub.

items.title: Air gapped, not data dark: how Bright Machines gives customers live factory dashboards without opening the plant
items.summary: Bright Machines successfully implemented a new architecture to give customers live factory dashboards without opening inbound access to their air-gapped plants. Announced in November 2026 by engineering authors including Jitesh Soni, Anup Chatterjee, and othe…
items.fullStory:
Bright Machines successfully implemented a new architecture to give customers live factory dashboards without opening inbound access to their air-gapped plants. Announced in November 2026 by engineering authors including Jitesh Soni, Anup Chatterjee, and others, the project replaced a complex nine-service pipeline with a unified, governed platform utilizing Debezium, Apache Iceberg, AWS Glue, and Databricks Unity Catalog federation.

The old architecture struggled with schema evolution, missing monitoring, and inadequate data governance, requiring manual ETL jobs that took hours or days. The new pipeline captures PostgreSQL changes at the factory edge using Debezium Server, writes them as Apache Iceberg tables to a local object store, and sends them out through a single auditable outbound path. Unity Catalog federation over AWS Glue enables Databricks to read the data in place without data duplication, while Databricks SQL and AI/BI Dashboards serve role-based insights to internal teams and external customers.

Following a pilot on a proof-of-concept line and a hard cutover, the new system achieved impressive performance metrics. Data committed on the assembly line is queryable in Databricks within one to two minutes, dashboards refresh every ten minutes, and a heartbeat check detects broken pipelines in under thirty minutes instead of days. The first customer-visible dashboard went live roughly two months after kickoff, eliminating the need to manually rerun and email on-prem reports.

items.title: BotPsy: On-Device Personal Assistant with a Sub-Billion-Parameter Agentic Language Model
items.summary: On November 11, 2026, Tether AI Research announced the release of BotPsy, a 0.8B-parameter agentic language model built on top of Qwen3.5-0.8B and designed specifically for on-device personal assistant tasks and function calling. The model was developed to ad…
items.fullStory:
On November 11, 2026, Tether AI Research announced the release of BotPsy, a 0.8B-parameter agentic language model built on top of Qwen3.5-0.8B and designed specifically for on-device personal assistant tasks and function calling. The model was developed to address the high operational costs, privacy risks, and lack of customization associated with frontier cloud LLMs, providing a performant, self-hosted alternative that can run locally on user hardware.

BotPsy was trained through a four-stage process consisting of Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT), Multi-teacher On-Policy Distillation (MOPD) using three specialist Qwen3.5-4B teachers, and two rounds of Reinforcement Learning (RL) powered by rule-based and environment verifiers. According to Tether, the model achieves state-of-the-art tool-use and agentic performance for its weight class, outperforming every model tested up to 1.2B parameters across six benchmarks including BFCL v4, ACEBench, and τ-bench. Notably, BotPsy also outperformed its larger sibling, Qwen3.5-2B-Think, on five of those six benchmarks while maintaining a lower unsafe response rate in automated red-teaming.

Published under the Apache 2.0 license, BotPsy is available in bf16, Q8, and Q4 precisions as Hugging Face safetensors and GGUF files compatible with the QVAC SDK and llama.cpp. Future development plans from Tether Data include expanding on-device agentic capabilities, enhancing decentralized peer-to-peer queries via Hypersearch, introducing local fine-tuning through QVAC Fabric, and supporting secure agent-to-agent communication across local networks.
items.whyItMatters: BotPsy demonstrates that sub-billion-parameter language models can achieve state-of-the-art tool-use and agentic performance, lowering the cost and privacy barriers for deploying capable AI assistants locally on-device.

items.title: Token Pooling-Aware Training for Multi-Vector Embedding Models
items.summary: On November 11, 2026, Hugging Face published an update detailing token pooling-aware training for multi-vector embedding models, written by Tom Aarsen. Multi-vector models like ColBERT provide expressive search capabilities by giving each query token an oppor…
items.fullStory:
On November 11, 2026, Hugging Face published an update detailing token pooling-aware training for multi-vector embedding models, written by Tom Aarsen. Multi-vector models like ColBERT provide expressive search capabilities by giving each query token an opportunity to find a match in a document, but this creates massive storage requirements. For example, storing 200 vectors of 128 dimensions per document across a million documents requires 12.8 GB of quantized residuals. Token pooling reduces this footprint by merging similar token vectors, but aggressive compression can cause the model to lose useful information.

To address this, token pooling-aware training teaches the encoder to preserve important information when vectors are merged, using hierarchical clustering methods like Ward's method to group similar embeddings by their mean. In the blog post's example, a normally trained model with a pool factor of 4 retains 94.6% of its unpooled NanoBEIR nDCG@10 while achieving a 4x reduction in document vectors, whereas token pooling-aware training raises that retention to 97.8% at the same storage budget. The training approach applies a combined loss function that averages the unpooled retrieval loss and the pooled retrieval loss, utilizing a straight-through estimator to pass gradients back to member tokens.

Developers can implement this functionality using Sentence Transformers via the MultiVectorTokenPoolingLoss wrapper alongside HierarchicalTokenPooling. The article also provides implementation details for calibrating adaptive pooling to target specific average token counts and outlines optional kernel acceleration to speed up MaxSim scoring and Ward clustering. Users can run training scripts locally using uv or execute them on a cloud GPU using Hugging Face Jobs with an A10G small flavor and a four-hour timeout.
items.whyItMatters: Token pooling-aware training significantly improves document retrieval quality while drastically reducing the storage footprint of multi-vector embedding models. This makes large-scale semantic search architectures much more efficient and cost-effective to deploy in production.

items.title: Decision Models in Hugging Face
items.summary: On November 10, 2026, Hugging Face published an article detailing "Decision Models" written by Aritra Roy Gosthipaty, Lysandre, Pedro Cuenca, and Tom Aarsen. The article introduces decision models as an alternative to large language models for tasks that do n…
items.fullStory:
On November 10, 2026, Hugging Face published an article detailing "Decision Models" written by Aritra Roy Gosthipaty, Lysandre, Pedro Cuenca, and Tom Aarsen. The article introduces decision models as an alternative to large language models for tasks that do not require generating text, such as routing customer support messages, scoring urgency, or evaluating yes/no probabilities.

Unlike traditional text-generating LLMs that require parsing JSON outputs or relying on constrained decoding to enforce structural constraints, decision models evaluate a state and a set of predefined questions and allowed answers to return structured decisions with probability distributions. The article compares decision models to traditional classification and zero-shot classification, noting that decision models natively support multiple typed questions, ordered scoring, and runtime-defined labels.

The interface for a decision model consists of a state (which can be a string, JSON object, or multi-modal input) and questions using three fundamental primitives: choice, score, and noul. The article provides code examples using the Hugging Face transformers pipeline with models like autotrust/GEV-26B-Decide to demonstrate how developers can obtain confidence scores, probabilities, and expected values directly without autoregressive token generation.
items.whyItMatters: Decision models offer a more efficient, structurally reliable alternative to LLMs for classification, routing, and structured evaluation tasks by returning direct probability distributions rather than generating free-form text.

items.title: Accelerate GPU training on Unity Catalog tables with UCDataset
items.summary: On November 9, 2026, Databricks Engineering announced the release of UCDataset (Unity Catalog Dataset) in Beta on AI Runtime, a native data loader designed to accelerate GPU training on Unity Catalog tables. Authored by John Spencer, Milan Stefanovic, Bruce F…
items.fullStory:
On November 9, 2026, Databricks Engineering announced the release of UCDataset (Unity Catalog Dataset) in Beta on AI Runtime, a native data loader designed to accelerate GPU training on Unity Catalog tables. Authored by John Spencer, Milan Stefanovic, Bruce Fontaine, and Tejas Sundaresan, the announcement highlights that UCDataset streams training data directly from Unity Catalog tables to GPUs, eliminating the need for slow, tedious exports to Parquet, memory-heavy pandas loading, or warehouse-throttled streaming.

According to the blog post, UCDataset plugs directly into standard PyTorch training loops, automatically handling multi-GPU data sharding without requiring custom sharding or sampler code. In simulated production benchmarks streaming a 300 GB feature table across 8 NVIDIA H100 GPUs to train a recommendation model, UCDataset achieved a 10x improvement in training time compared to reading from an exported Parquet copy. The tool reads table files directly from cloud storage, applies filters and deletion vectors dynamically as data is read, and automatically includes newly appended rows on subsequent runs.

Furthermore, the tool maintains end-to-end governance by enforcing standard Unity Catalog permissions, with training jobs reading data as the executing identity. For unstructured data or multimodal training, Databricks also offers UCVolumeDataset and plans to support FILE types for images, audio, and documents. Users can get started by installing the package via `pip install databricks-uc-dataset`, though the beta currently cannot read tables with existing row filters or column masks.
items.whyItMatters: UCDataset eliminates expensive data plumbing and export bottlenecks by streaming governed Delta tables directly into distributed PyTorch training loops, cutting training times by up to 10x.

items.title: Your Experts Have Partners. There's HOPE for Keeping Them Together
items.summary: On November 9, 2026, researchers Alex M. Tseng and Luca Zancato published an article introducing HOPE (Higher-Order Pruning of Experts), a second-order pruning method designed for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) large language models. Standard MoE models scale param…
items.fullStory:
On November 9, 2026, researchers Alex M. Tseng and Luca Zancato published an article introducing HOPE (Higher-Order Pruning of Experts), a second-order pruning method designed for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) large language models. Standard MoE models scale parameters into the hundreds of billions, but their expert MLPs create a memory bottleneck because they must occupy memory at inference time even when 95% of them remain idle for any given token. While first-order pruning methods independently score and delete the least useful experts based on scalar importance, they ignore cooperative groups of co-activated experts, leading to performance drops at aggressive pruning rates.

HOPE addresses this limitation by defining a tractable surrogate that upper-bounds the pruning error and naturally produces cross-terms accounting for pairwise expert interactions. By minimizing the expectation of this surrogate over a calibration dataset, HOPE solves a quadratic program using an F-matrix whose off-diagonal entries capture pairwise cooperative contributions. According to the authors, the diagonal of the F-matrix recovers previous first-order rankings like REAP with a Spearman rho of 0.988, meaning all performance gains come directly from incorporating these second-order interaction terms. Solving the quadratic program adds a negligible overhead of 1 to 2 seconds per layer.

The researchers evaluated HOPE across three models—Qwen3.5-122B, Qwen3.5-35B, and GLM-4.5-Air—using Evol-CodeAlpaca and SWE-Bench Verified calibration datasets and benchmarks including the Tulu3 suite and SWE-Bench Pro. Across all conditions, HOPE achieved the best average rank of 2.07 out of five methods and secured top-1 finishes in 39% of conditions. At an aggressive 50% pruning rate, HOPE's average rank improved to 1.58 compared to 2.42 for the next-best method, REAP. On Qwen3.5-35B-A3B at 50% pruning, a model pruned with HOPE achieved a score of 42.3 on SWE-Bench Pro, matching the unpruned model's 41.8, whereas REAP dropped to 36.2.
items.whyItMatters: HOPE significantly reduces the massive memory footprint of Mixture-of-Experts language models at high pruning rates without sacrificing performance on complex tasks like agentic coding.
items.whoIsAffected: AI researchers, machine learning engineers, and developers optimizing large language models for inference efficiency.
